blocks.html: Dr. McCullough is a well-respected North Texas cardiologist with impeccable academic credentials.  He is a full professor of medicine at Texas A&M College of Medicine in Dallas.  Dr. McCullough is an internist, cardiologist, epidemiologist, and holds a Master of Public Health degree.  He is known as one of the top five most-published medical researchers in the United States and is the editor of two medical journals.
Below are six items Dr. McCullough recommends keeping in your over-the-counter toolbox to help your immune system fight the effects of the COVID-19 virus:

items: Vitamin D 5,000 IU/day, Increased to 20,000 IU/day during active treatment
Quercetin, 500 mg a day for prevention, 500mg/day for active treatment
Famotidine or Pepcid at a high dose, 80 mg/day active treatment

blocks.html: In addition to these recommendations, the providers at Victory Medical provide prescription antivirals that assist in the treatment of the Omicron variants.
What are the types of COVID testing you offer?
We currently offer two types of COVID testing.

items: Molecular (PCR) Test Collected onsite and sent out to participating laboratory Results: Currently 5-7 business days (due to high demand)

blocks.html: PCR testing is performed with a nasopharyngeal swab. This tests for ACTIVE infection and detects viral genetic material (RNA). It is considered very accurate however, results are not immediately available. As of October 2020, results are taking 5-7 days. If you have symptoms, and antibody tests are negative, you should consider a PCR test.
Antigen testing is performed with a nasopharyngeal swab. This tests for ACTIVE infection. If you have symptoms, and antigen tests are negative, you should consider a PCR test as a follow up measure.

Is antibody testing right for me if I have symptoms?
We are unable to diagnose COVID-19 based solely on antibody test results. Patients that are currently experiencing symptoms or that have seen a Victory provider will be encouraged to have PCR molecular nasal swab testing.

What are the COVID symptoms I should look for?
COVID-19 symptoms* include the following:

items:
Fever or chills
Cough
Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Fatigue
Muscle or body aches
Headache
New loss of taste or smell
Sore throat
Congestion or runny nose
Nausea or vomiting
Diarrhea

blocks.html: *This does not include all possible symptoms. We will update as information becomes available from the CDC.
What is the cost of COVID testing?
The cost will range from $42-$56 depending if you have insurance and based on your specific insurance coverage allowable.
Can I schedule an appointment for COVID testing?

We are currently accepting walk-ins and appointments for COVID testing in the office. If you have tested positive with an over-the-counter test and are seeking treatment options but prefer not to come in person, we offer virtual visits as well.
Can I be seen as a walk-in and what are your walk-in hours?
If you are having COVID-19 related symptoms, we encourage you to walk-in. We see walk-ins during our regular business hours at both locations:
• 4303 Victory Drive: (M-F 8am-7pm), (Sat 9am-5pm), (Sun Noon-5pm)
• 3811 Bee Caves Rd: (M-Th 8am-7pm), (F-8am-5pm), (Sat 9am-5pm)
My PCR Nasal swab test is PENDING or POSITIVE , what do I do now?
If you are HAVING SYMPTOMS, you may discontinue isolation when:
• At least 5 days have passed since the date of their first positive COVID-19 diagnostic test AND fever free for 24 hours.
• Have had no subsequent illness and you remain asymptomatic.

CLINIC PRECAUTIONS and SAFETY GUIDELINES BEING FOLLOWED:

items: We have set up a check-in/screening station for patients outside of the office in order to separate sick patients from all other issues. Patients presenting with at-risk symptoms or have a positive screening are asked to remain in their car to wait to be seen and then escorted to a specific area within the building for evaluation and treatment.
We are thoroughly and regularly cleaning all surfaces in common areas and reception desks throughout the day with hospital grade disinfectant.
Rooms are sanitized between each patient.
Frequently touched items such as magazines, brochures, water fountains, etc have been removed from waiting and patient exam rooms.
Tape marks have been placed on the floor and waiting room chairs have been spread out to provide for recommended social distancing.
Victory team members are provided with personal protective equipment (when available) as recommended by the CDC and OSHA.
Our nightly cleaning crew utilizes hospital-grade disinfectant to wipe down all surfaces.
Interior doors are being propped open to minimize the need for hand to surface contact.
Water fountain service has been discontinued, and water available upon request.
